fact: Tanzania is stepping up efforts to issue the Jamii Namba, a number assigned from birth through civil registration, to children, with a legal framework being prepared.
The Daily News says the Home Affairs budget continues the Jamii Namba rollout, a system designed to give every citizen a unique identification number from birth, kept for life.
The Minister of Home Affairs told Parliament in the 2026/27 budget speech that NIDA expects to start registering children from birth to give a unique number called Jamii Namba.

The government has completed preparations for a pilot issuing Jamii Namba unique ID numbers to children from birth on birth certificates in Rungwe, Kilolo and Unguja South, once legal arrangements are completed, per the Deputy Minister.
The NIDA Director General says government plans a draft Child Registration Act in the next parliamentary session to empower NIDA to register children from birth.

NIDA's Director General says an Infant Registration Bill, to be tabled from 27 January 2026, would register children at birth and assign a unique identification number used to issue a national digital ID card at 18.
The NIDA Director said a child-identification plan, registering children with NIDA from birth, is under pilot in three districts.
The Home Affairs Minister said preparations are underway to register children so that every Tanzanian has a National Identification Number.
NIDA says the national ID is issued only from age 18, leaving children without an identity number for nearly two decades.
